For someone who has never owned a gun, what's a good handgun that has enough stopping power to put down a feral beast, but also holds enough rounds to handle a feral pack if the need arises?

It really depends on personal preference. Go to your local gun range, take a gun safety class, rent a few different guns and see what you are most comfortable with. 9mm ammo is cheaper and lighter, so a 9mm weapon will usually hold more rounds than say a .45. In the real world, the ammo caliber matters very little compared to the aim and training of the shooter. Larger calibers usually have more recoil, which can make aiming multiple shots fired in quick succession trickier. Remember, you can always carry multiple magazines too so mag capacity is not the end all be all of how well the weapon will work on large groups of hostiles. Well trained individuals are able to swap mags in a few seconds or less. Again, proper training is most important here. A well trained individual can conceivably take down 6 untrained armed persons with 7 rounds. That said, can you envision being attacked by more than a few hostiles at once? If you can you might want to opt for something larger than a pistol, such as an AR-15.

Personally, I like Colt 1911s. My favorite is the .45 Combat Elite, although I also like the Rail Gun and the Special Combat Government. Like I said, however, it all depends on how the gun feels in your hands and how accurate you are with it. With firearms, what works for one person may not necessarily work for the next. Head down to your local range, or better yet ask a friend who is familiar with handguns to show you the ropes. You should really try out a few of the more popular types of pistols to see what suits you before buying.

You should also try out a Glock. I don't own one myself, and many people don't like the idea of a weapon with a polymer frame but they're very reliable and affordable. Many law enforcement agencies swear by them, i believe it's the most widely used brand by police departments.

Also, for sheer stopping power, you might want to consider a 12 gauge shotgun, you can get a good one relatively cheaply and they'll stop a charging bear in its tracks. If you want something smaller and you find out you like the feel of a revolver, you might want to check out the Taurus Judge. It can shoot .45acp rounds and .410 shotgun shells, which makes it really versatile.
That's excellent advice. I went the inexpensive route. I carry a Glock 23 with 13 Hornady Critical Defense rounds 100% of the time IWB. I never leave home without it, I mean never.
